sets.name: 2-letter words
sets.tip: The single most valuable list in Scrabble. Learn them letter by letter: say every 2 that contains A, then B, and so on. Know the hooks too: they let you play parallel to existing words.

sets.name: 3-letter words
sets.tip: Learn them in small daily batches, most probable racks first. Read the definitions, because a meaning (even a silly one) makes a word much easier to recall. The hooks show which 4s each 3 can become.

sets.name: JQXZ 4-letter words
sets.tip: The power tiles score big on short words. Learn each tile as a family (all the J 4s, then Q, X and Z) and look for the patterns, like the -IZ and -AX endings.

sets.name: Three-vowel 4s
sets.tip: Your rescue list for when the rack is full of vowels. Words like AEON, EUOI and OUZO dump three or more vowels in one go.

sets.name: Q without U
sets.tip: These save you when you draw a Q with no U. Start with QI, QAT, QADI, QAID and QOPH, then add the longer ones. Their plurals (QATS, QAIDS) count too.

sets.name: Top 100 7s
sets.tip: These are the 100 seven-letter racks you are most likely to draw, so they are the bingos you will see most often. Learn each rack with all its anagrams. Say the letters, find every word, and repeat.

sets.name: Top 100 8s
sets.tip: The 100 most likely eight-letter bingos, which you play through a tile already on the board. Learn them as anagram sets, just like the 7s.
